create.name: Richard Tarnas
create.bio:
A cultural historian and philosopher, Richard Tarnas draws together the history of ideas, depth psychology and archetypal astrology. At CIIS in San Francisco (the California Institute of Integral Studies) he founded the Philosophy, Cosmology, and Consciousness programme and taught there for some thirty years, on the evolution of consciousness, Jungian and archetypal psychology and archetypal cosmology; he is now Professor Emeritus. Earlier, he spent ten years at Esalen Institute in Big Sur, rising to director of programmes and education, and he has been a regular lecturer at Pacifica Graduate Institute.

The Passion of the Western Mind, widely used in universities, follows Western thought from ancient Greece into the postmodern era. In Cosmos and Psyche: Intimations of a New World View he argues for correlations between planetary cycles and archetypal patterns, both in history and in individual lives; the Scientific and Medical Network named it its Book of the Year. Prometheus the Awakener, a shorter essay, looks at the archetype of Uranus. He was once president of the International Transpersonal Association. These days he teaches mostly online, with courses at the Kosmos Institute and, alongside Stanislav Grof, the Psyche & Cosmos programmes on The Shift Network.

books.title: The Passion of the Western Mind: Understanding the Ideas that Have Shaped Our World View
books.author: Richard Tarnas
books.description: A narrative history of Western thought from the ancient Greeks through the Middle Ages, the Renaissance and the Scientific Revolution to the postmodern age. It traces how changing ideas about the cosmos, the divine and the human have shaped the modern world view.

books.title: Cosmos and Psyche: Intimations of a New World View
books.author: Richard Tarnas
books.description: Tarnas sets out evidence for meaningful correspondences between planetary alignments and archetypal patterns in cultural history and in individual lives. The book draws on depth psychology and the history of ideas to argue for a re-enchanted, participatory view of the cosmos.

books.title: Prometheus the Awakener: An Essay on the Archetypal Meaning of the Planet Uranus
books.author: Richard Tarnas
books.description: A short essay arguing that the planet Uranus corresponds to the archetype of Prometheus: rebellion, sudden breakthroughs, creative genius and liberation. It illustrates the idea through the lives of individuals and the timing of historical events.

courses.title: Psyche & Cosmos
courses.description: An eight-module self-paced course with Richard Tarnas and Stanislav Grof introducing archetypal astrology. It links planetary cycles with depth psychology and Grof's research into non-ordinary states, as a way of understanding the patterns of a life.

courses.title: The Psyche & Cosmos Advanced Program
courses.description: Fourteen recorded 90-minute modules and four Q&A sessions with Richard Tarnas and Stanislav Grof, with the introductory Psyche & Cosmos course included. Students learn to calculate and interpret their own transits and explore synchronicity, history and the arts through an archetypal lens.

courses.title: Cosmos and Psyche: Archetypal Astrology and a Depth Understanding of History
courses.description: A nine-week live online course with the Kosmos Institute based on his book Cosmos and Psyche, meeting on Saturdays. It covers the core ideas of archetypal astrology, planetary cycles in history, and Jungian archetypes and synchronicity, with lifetime access to the recordings.

courses.title: The Passion of the Western Mind: A Brief History of the Western World View
courses.description: An on-demand nine-week course surveying the evolution of the Western world view from ancient Greece and Israel to the postmodern present. Lectures follow how each age understood the cosmos, the divine and the human.

courses.title: On the Pantheon of the Planetary Archetypes: An Evening with Richard Tarnas
courses.description: A two-hour online talk for CIIS Public Programs on the archetypal meanings of the Sun, Moon and planets. It looks at how these archetypes appear in natal charts and world transits, and how self-awareness shapes the way they are lived.

free_resources.title: Introduction to Archetypal Astrology
free_resources.description: A short essay written in 1987 as background for people about to receive a natal chart and transit reading. It explains the basic ideas of archetypal astrology in plain terms.

free_resources.title: Is the Modern Psyche Undergoing a Rite of Passage?
free_resources.description: An essay based on his lectures of the late 1990s, asking whether the turmoil of the modern era can be understood as a collective initiation. It has been published in several journals and anthologies.

free_resources.title: Archetypal Cosmology: Past and Present
free_resources.description: An essay on the origins and history of archetypal cosmology. It traces the field from its roots to its present form as an academic discipline.

free_resources.title: Two Suitors: A Parable
free_resources.description: A free excerpt from Cosmos and Psyche. Told as a parable, it compares two contrasting ways of approaching and knowing the universe.

sprint.tier_evidence: No social accounts of his own found (his site cosmosandpsyche.com links none; the YouTube talks are all on other people's channels) → 0 readable followers → local_hero
flags: Tier is local_hero only because he has no social accounts; his reputation (The Passion of the Western Mind is a long-standing university text) is much bigger than that, so a human may want to override the tier.
The email is his institutional CIIS address (Professor Emeritus) from the CIIS faculty directory; his own website publishes no email or contact form.
Both Shift courses are co-taught with Stanislav Grof, who already has a Spiritpedia listing (stanislav-grof).
Becca Tarnas (sprint rank 95) is his daughter and works in the same field; possible overlap of items.

Several videos are on channels that look like fan archives or reuploads (ArchetypalView, Intellectual Deep Web); they are lectures and interviews where he is the speaker, but the uploaders may not be the rights holders.
Shift prices are current sale prices: Psyche & Cosmos $247 USD (regular $297 USD); Advanced Program $1097 USD.
left_out: Psyche Unbound: Essays in Honor of Stanislav Grof (he is co-editor, not author).
Prometheus the Awakener 2018 revised edition (ISBN-10 0882140687): its Amazon /dp/ page returned an error, so the 1995 edition's listing (0882142216) is used.
Richard Tarnas on the Planets in 2024 (CIIS, yXUXRxH2V6A): dated forecast.
ArchetypalView reupload of the 2025 CIIS lecture (upW6FTCR1z8): the CIIS Public Programs original is used instead.
His new Shift live course beginning September 2027 has no page or URL yet.
Other essays on cosmosandpsyche.com (Esalen prose poem, Hillman tribute, ten most influential books) are not teaching resources.
